body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\), determine explicit rate functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) such that \(R_d(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) uniformly over every legal \(K=K_N\), including exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition. The lower-bound branch must choose the finite-support simultaneous family so that \(\Delta_{N,K}\) matches the claimed rate, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) certifies the endpoint separation against every rematching column; its ordered low-versus-high version must also support the one-sided length converse. The upper-bound branch must construct a computable estimator and uniformly honest lower bound attaining the respective rates, or prove a sharper shared-geometric dual bound if the simultaneous family cannot achieve the required separation.
body.justification: After removing every subsequence with a positive lower bound on \(K_N/N^{q_d}\), the kernel is the exact estimation and ordered one-sided frontier on all remaining small-ratio subsequences, including those inside irregular arrays.
body.gap: Exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms, the missing arm factor, mixture indistinguishability, and ordered separation resistant to every rematching column remain unresolved.
body.consumer: A solution would combine with the proved positive-lower-bound subsequences to complete the decision-theoretic rate account for every legal array.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided lower bounds, or a sharper shared-geometric upper bound, on every subsequence for which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) tends to zero, including the exact fixed-\(K\) logarithm and every transition; combine these with the already solved positive-lower-bound subsequences of each irregular legal array.
obligation.obstruction: The available nonparametric converse is the embedded two-margin order \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\), while the theoretical plug-in upper contribution is \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). No simultaneous-marginal family has yet certified an ordered endpoint separation of the missing order while maintaining mixture total variation at most \(1/4\) and nonnegative reduced-cost slack against every rematching column, and no sharper aggregate bound for the jointly conjugate potentials is available.
obligation.attempted: The exact residual cap, optimal-support diameter, common-support empirical interpolation, two-margin reduction, ordered Bernoulli pair, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) results, rational certified algorithm, sparse-arm and parity examples, and fixed-dimensional orthogonal constructions have been exhausted. They settle every positive-lower-bound subsequence but do not close the small-ratio arm-factor or logarithmic gap.
obligation.partial_result:
For every balanced array under the maintained product experiment and unit-ball support, the already proved sandwich is
\[
c_d\max\left\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\right\}
\le R_d(N,K)
\le C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
The already proved one-sided result is
\[
c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}
\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
The upper length bound is attained by \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\), a theoretical uniformly calibrated rule whose constant \(C_d\) is proved to exist but is not numerically supplied. Independently, \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is fully specified, requires no transport computation, is uniformly honest, and obeys the valid baseline upper length order \(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2\). Both decision risks are of exact order \(N^{-1/2}\) on every subsequence for which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) is bounded below by a positive constant, where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). Consequently, if a legal array has \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\), only its subsequences with ratio tending to zero remain unresolved; its positive-lower-bound subsequences are already settled. The rational-grid empirical multi-marginal transport algorithm separately returns primal and dual certificates with any rational requested width \(\epsilon\) in time polynomial in \(N\) and \((K/\epsilon)^d\). The missing result is a matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided converse, or a sharper aggregate upper bound, on every small-ratio subsequence, including fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition.
